gen_risks.description: DSR design and rollout may be delayed because past registry attempts failed due to poor data quality and weak institutional mandate.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct a comprehensive data audit, secure dedicated funding for data cleaning, and establish a clear governance structure with strict timelines.
gen_risks.evidence: Past attempts at social registry did not materialize due to incomplete and outdated data, lag in MIS development, early cuts in funding, and lack of institutional mandate.

gen_risks.description: MIS and data platforms could experience downtime despite disaster‑recovery centres.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement regular disaster‑recovery testing, maintain backup power supplies, and enforce service‑level agreements with the data‑center providers.
gen_risks.evidence: All MIS/data platforms will be housed inside the National Data Centers... disaster recovery centers will ensure that the MIS shall continue running uninterrupted even if the main servers are damaged.

gen_risks.description: Integrating the DSR with existing ISPMIS and other beneficiary databases may encounter technical difficulties.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop a detailed integration roadmap, pilot the interface in selected Upazilas, and allocate technical assistance for system testing.
gen_risks.evidence: The final design will leverage the existing Integrated Social Protection MIS (ISPMIS) and will support linkages between existing cash transfer beneficiary databases.

gen_risks.description: Currency and foreign‑exchange fluctuations could increase project costs in local currency.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain an FX buffer, use hedging instruments where feasible, and regularly review the budget against exchange‑rate movements.
gen_risks.evidence: FX reserves stood at US$19.9 billion (approximately 3.3 months of prospective imports).

gen_risks.description: Financing may be withheld if performance‑based condition targets are not achieved.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen monitoring systems, provide early‑warning dashboards, and deliver capacity‑building to ensure timely achievement of PBC targets.
gen_risks.evidence: Financing would be disbursed against achievement of PBCs... If targets not met, funds not released.

gen_risks.description: Delay in establishing the PIU, DSR coordination unit and steering committee as required by legal covenants.
gen_risks.mitigation: Assign senior officials with clear accountability, track set‑up milestones weekly, and include covenant compliance clauses in contracts.
gen_risks.evidence: Recipient shall establish within six months... DSR steering committee within two months... PIU will be set up at the DSS.

gen_risks.description: Phase‑wise rollout of the DSR may be slower than planned, reducing expected coverage gains.
gen_risks.mitigation: Create a realistic rollout schedule with buffer periods, conduct parallel pilots, and allocate contingency funds for accelerated deployment if needed.
gen_risks.evidence: Phase‑wise rollout... first phase four of the largest life‑cycle‑based cash transfer programs have been selected to be onboarded.

gen_risks.description: Coordination gaps among ministries, FD, DSS and partners could impede implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Formalise MoUs, establish a joint steering committee with regular meetings, and use a shared project‑management portal for transparency.
gen_risks.evidence: Coordination committee will be established... implementation units... MoUs with key line ministries.

gen_risks.description: Dependence on EU and GIZ complementary activities may lead to mis‑alignment or duplication.
gen_risks.mitigation: Align work plans through joint planning workshops and conduct periodic joint monitoring to ensure synergy.
gen_risks.evidence: EU has been investing... GIZ has been working with the DSS... coordination will be critical to minimize duplication.

gen_risks.description: Recent political transition creates macro‑economic and policy uncertainty.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain continuous dialogue with all political factions, embed flexibility in work plans, and monitor policy changes closely.
gen_risks.evidence: Interim government was sworn in on August 8, 2024... significant downside risks and uncertainty remain.

gen_risks.description: Failure to comply with legal covenants (e.g., establishing required units) could trigger project suspension.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a covenant‑compliance tracker, conduct quarterly reviews, and apply corrective actions promptly.
gen_risks.evidence: Legal covenants require establishment of PIU, DSR coordination unit, DSR steering committee within specified timeframes.

gen_risks.description: Climate‑related floods or cyclones may disrupt field activities, data collection and beneficiary registration.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilise remote/online registration channels, pre‑position field kits in high‑risk districts, and design climate‑resilient field procedures.
gen_risks.evidence: Bangladesh faces high level of vulnerability to climate change... floods affect more than 1 million people annually.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient capacity of DSS staff to operate the DSR and follow new guidelines.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deliver comprehensive training, certify staff, and provide ongoing technical support and refresher courses.
gen_risks.evidence: Each Upazila in the country has at least one DSS personnel who has been trained on the updated business processes under the guidelines for DSS implementation of DSR.

gen_risks.description: Complex fiduciary arrangements may lead to weak internal controls and audit gaps.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire experienced FM consultants, strengthen iBAS integration, and conduct annual risk‑based internal audits by independent firms.
gen_risks.evidence: From the FM perspective, the project design is complex... mitigation measures include hiring additional capacity, training, and close monitoring.

gen_risks.description: High inflation could erode the real value of cash‑transfer benefits and increase project costs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement the benefit‑adequacy framework with index‑linking to CPI or HIES and review benefit levels annually or when inflation exceeds thresholds.
gen_risks.evidence: Inflation remained elevated, reaching 9.9% in January 2025.

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk is Substantial. Safety and security concerns persist, despite the priority placed by the interim government on law and order. The interim government is implementing critical reforms before holding elections; reaching a consensus on reforms and the announcement of the election date could heighten political tensions among political parties and the interim government.
gt_risks.mitigation: These risks will be mitigated during implementation through continuous engagement with all relevant government and nongovernmental entities, and dialogue with other stakeholders.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is Substantial. Downside risks have increased, related to uncertainties in the political process and the security situation which affects the recovery of economic activities. The financial sector remains vulnerable with deviations from international regulatory and supervisory standards and weak corporate governance. Despite recent improvements, the balance of payments remained in deficit and FX reserves remained under pressure.
gt_risks.mitigation: The macroeconomic risks are partially mitigated by the GoB's reform program, supported by International Monetary Fund arrangements, as well as ongoing World Bank and other development partners' policy lending. Data show consistent budgetary and political commitment to spending on safety nets across regimes in Bangladesh, with strong stakeholder consensus on ensuring a ring-fenced core budget for social assistance and livelihoods programs for the poorest.

gt_risks.description: The Fiduciary risk is rated Substantial due to the involvement of multiple implementing agencies (the DSS and FD), the complexity of activity selection, and intervention modalities. The project's residual procurement risk specifically is also rated Substantial, due to the complexity of procurement activities, multiagency coordination, and capacity limitations (para 56, part of the Fiduciary appraisal-summary discussion immediately preceding the Key Risks section).
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigation measures include hiring additional capacity, training, and close monitoring; considering satisfactory implementation of these measures, the residual fiduciary risk is assessed as Substantial and will be managed through proactive and continuous supervision and close dialogue with the GoB. Procurement-specific mitigation: hiring full-time procurement consultants for the DSS and FD; training on World Bank Procurement Regulations, STEP, and contract management; defining clear roles and streamlining approval processes; engaging IT procurement specialists and conducting early market assessments; using performance-based KPIs in contracts and including procurement consultants on bid evaluation committees; and establishing complaint registers at both agencies, with procurement not prior-reviewed by the Bank subject to regular fiduciary reviews and post-procurement review/audit by FAPAD.

gt_risks.description: The project presents a low environmental risk and a moderate social risk, resulting in an overall moderate environmental and social (ES) risk classification. Minor environmental concerns relate to potential e-waste generation from IT equipment and increased energy use. Social risks include potential exclusion of beneficiaries, inadequate consultation, and challenges in reaching remote and marginalized communities, including those who lack IT knowledge; there is also the likelihood of sexual exploitation and abuse/sexual harassment (SEA/SH) cases given the cash transfer modalities of the project and the interaction between service providers and beneficiaries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Waste management protocols and resource efficiency measures will prevent localized pollution. The project will establish a Digital Social Registry (DSR) to improve targeting and coverage, complemented by a robust outreach and monitoring program, and will include Stakeholder Engagement Plan provisions requiring community consultation and disclosure measures. The existing DSS grievance redress mechanism (GRM) will address complaints. An SEA/SH Action Plan will be developed including code of conduct, awareness raising, and GRM to address potential incidents. The project will partially rely on the borrower's ES management framework supplemented by gap-filling measures included in the POM.
